title: Missing tile warnings in TileMap dock display with wrong texture filter
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in latest commit on master: `v4.8.dev.custom_build [ca871ccc9]` ### System information Godot v4.8.dev (ca871ccc9) - macOS Sequoia (15.7.4) - Multi-window, 2 monitors (1920x1080 @ 60.00 Hz, 1920x1080 @ 60.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 (Apple9) - Apple M4 (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description TileMapLayer warning textures will inherit the texture_filter of the underlying TileMapLayer instead of always using a Linear filter. This results in grainy, pixelated warning textures whenever the filter is set to Nearest (for instance in ProjectSettings) which is a minor visual bug. Expected: Actual: The issue is that tile warning textures are drawn to `TileMapLayerEditor::custom_overlay`, which needs to inherit TileMapLayer's filter (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123692). These warning textures should never be displayed with a filter other than LINEAR. ### Steps to reproduce 1. In a brand new project create a scene, create a TileMapLayer node and create a tileset for it. 2. Place a given tile in the editor. 3. With the tile placed, navigate to the TileSet tab and delete that tile from the Tileset so that a warning texture appears. Navigate back to the TileMap tab to see the warning in the editor. 4. In the inspector, set TileMapLayer's `texture_filter` to Nearest. 5. Observe that the warning texture becomes pixelated and grainy. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) MRP instructions: Open the project and select either of the TileMapLayer nodes to view the correct version of the warning (with a linear filter), and the incorrect one (with the nearest filter). [mrp-tile-warning-texture-filter.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32586163/mrp-tile-warning-texture-filter.zip)
